candidates.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
candidates.why: The one Kyoto sight that is still worth it, but only early. It's free and open 24h. Arrive by about 07:00 (sunrise is about 07:00 in late Dec) and walk the torii tunnels up to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint, about 45 min up, before the 10:00–16:00 crush. The full loop of the mountain is about 4 km and takes 2h+. For 8 friends, Yotsutsuji is the sensible turnaround.
candidates.group_of_8: Fine. Paths get single-file at peak, so go early.

evidence.note: 4.6 from 92k reviews, open 24 hours
Quietest 6–9am. Peak is 10–16 on weekends. Mountain loop about 4 km, 2h+

candidates.name: Kiyomizu-dera & Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka
candidates.name_ja: 清水寺・三年坂・二年坂
candidates.why: The classic Kyoto view from the wooden stage. Gates open at 06:00, so go first thing, then walk down the Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka slopes before the shops open and the crowds arrive. By 10:00 it's a tourist trap, so treat it as an early stop only. It pairs with Fushimi Inari: Keihan from Fushimi-Inari to Kiyomizu-Gojo or Gion-Shijo is about 10 min.

evidence.note: Opens 6:00; closing time varies by season

candidates.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Togetsukyo
candidates.name_ja: 嵐山 竹林の小径・渡月橋
candidates.why: Stunning at 07:30 and a shoulder-to-shoulder selfie queue by 10:00. The path is public and open 24h. Do Togetsukyo Bridge at about 08:00, then the bamboo, then Tenryu-ji or Okochi Sanso if you want more. From Kujo: Hanshin or the Metro to Umeda, then Hankyu to Arashiyama (Hankyu 1-Day Pass ¥1,300 covers Umeda–Arashiyama–Kawaramachi). Note that the Arashiyama Hanatouro light-up ended in 2021 and its successor, Tsukitouro, runs in autumn, so there is no December night event.
candidates.group_of_8: Fine; go early or it's a crawl

candidates.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
candidates.why: A 30–40 min photo stop: postcard-perfect, but you only walk one loop. It doesn't open until 09:00, so it can't be a dawn stop. Do it right after Arashiyama (about 25 min by bus or taxi; a taxi split four ways is cheap for 8) and skip it if the day runs late.

evidence.note: Opens 9:00 (¥500); arrive at opening for fewer people

candidates.name: Nara Park (deer)
candidates.why: The deer are the highlight, and travellers who thought Nara was skippable say they were wrong. Buy shika senbei (deer crackers) and bow to the deer; they bow back and also headbutt. Get there by about 08:30, before the tour buses. Big win for a Kujo base: the Hanshin Namba Line from Kujo runs through to Kintetsu-Nara with no change (about 50 min). Kintetsu-Nara is the closer station to the park.

evidence.note: 4.6 from 77k reviews

candidates.name: Todai-ji (Great Buddha Hall)
candidates.why: The one paid sight in Nara you shouldn't skip: a 15 m bronze Buddha in one of the world's largest wooden halls. Crawling through the pillar hole is a group dare. Pair it with the deer and Nigatsu-do, a free hillside hall with a sunset view, then head back to Osaka by mid-afternoon. Kasuga Taisha is optional.

candidates.why: It's the 25th-anniversary winter season (13 Nov 2026–17 Jan 2027). There's a new night show, 'Light Up the Night ~Christmas Celebration~' in Gramercy Park (25 Nov–11 Jan, usually 17:30 and 19:30, about 30 min), plus the returning 'Joy of Lights' and the park's biggest-ever Universal Food Festival. It's only 1 stop from Kujo to Nishikujo on Hanshin, then the JR Yumesaki Line to Universal City (about 15 min door to door). Go Mon 21 or Tue 22 Dec. Christmas Eve and Day are forecast to be crowded, school holidays start, and last year's ticket price rose about ¥1,000 from 24 Dec.

candidates.name: OSAKA Hikari Renaissance (Nakanoshima)
candidates.name_ja: OSAKA光のルネサンス2026（中之島）
candidates.why: Osaka's flagship Christmas light show runs 11–25 Dec 2026, so Christmas Eve and Christmas night are its final nights. The centrepiece is projection mapping on the 1918 Central Public Hall. It's free and walkable from Yodoyabashi or Kitahama, and it continues straight onto the Midosuji Illumination. Expect big crowds on 24–25 Dec, so go 21–23 Dec if you want space.

candidates.name: Osaka Castle Main Tower
candidates.why: The inside is a modern museum. The worth-it part is the grounds, the moats and the rooftop view, and those are free. Do it on an Osaka Amazing Pass day: the main tower and the Gozabune moat boat (10:00–16:30) are both included. Closed 28 Dec–1 Jan, which doesn't matter for 21–26 Dec.

candidates.name: Spa World
candidates.name_ja: スパワールド 世界の大温泉
candidates.why: Osaka's cheap and cheerful onsen theme park, with themed European and Asian bath floors (they swap men and women monthly) and a swimsuit pool with slides that the whole group can use together. It's the classic post-Shinsekai soak. Strict no-tattoo rule, which covers temporary tattoos and stickers. Staying past midnight adds a ¥1,300 surcharge plus bath tax, so leave before 24:00 or treat it as a cheap crash spot. Don't go in drunk.

notes: Osaka · sights: AREA LOGIC (Osaka base, Kujo; 21 Dec Mon to 26 Dec Sat 2026). Kujo is on both the Osaka Metro Chuo Line and the Hanshin Namba Line, which is unusually well connected for day trips: Hanshin through-trains run to Kintetsu-Nara with no change; 1 stop to Nishikujo then JR Yumesaki Line for USJ; 1 stop to Bentencho (Solaniwa onsen); 3 to Osakako (Kaiyukan). Suggested pairing: (1) USJ on Mon 21 or Tue 22; avoid 24–25 Dec, which are crowded and pricier, with school holidays starting. (2) Kyoto east day: Fushimi Inari at 06:30–07:00, then Keihan to Kiyomizu and Higashiyama by 08:30–09:00, Gion at midday. Keihan Kyoto-Osaka pass ¥1,650 vs ¥490 single from Yodoyabashi, so it only pays with 4+ rides. (3) Kyoto west day: Hankyu 1-Day ¥1,300 to Arashiyama by 07:30, then Kinkaku-ji at 09:00. Alternatively combine Arashiyama with Nara. (4) Nara half-day by Hanshin/Kintetsu: deer and Todai-ji 08:30–13:00, back for an Osaka evening. (5) Osaka Amazing Pass day (¥3,500 1-day / ¥5,000 2-day): Osaka Castle and Gozabune in the morning, Umeda Sky before 15:00 (pass entry cutoff), Tsutenkaku, then the Tombori cruise at night. It pays for itself with 3 or more paid sights. Christmas lights: Hikari Renaissance (Nakanoshima, 11–25 Dec, so it ends Christmas night) plus Midosuji Illumination (to 31 Dec, lit until 01:00) make one free evening walk from Yodoyabashi to Namba that ends in Dotonbori for nightlife (w2). Umeda Sky Christmas runs to 25 Dec. KOBE LUMINARIE is NOT on in December: since 2024 it moved to late Jan/early Feb (2026 edition was 30 Jan–8 Feb), so skip Kobe for lights. Arashiyama Hanatouro ended in 2021, and the Osaka Castle Illuminage 2026–27 dates are not yet announced (2025–26 ran 1 Nov–1 Feb, ¥2,000). PASSES: the JR paper Kansai Area Pass stopped selling on 30 Sep 2026. The WEST QR version is sold only by agencies outside Japan, so buy before flying if you want it, though it's rarely worth it from Kujo, which is a private-railway base. The KANSAI RAILWAY PASS (2-day ¥5,600, non-consecutive days) usually does NOT beat ICOCA for one Kyoto day plus one Nara day from Kujo. Default to ICOCA plus single-company day passes (Hankyu ¥1,300, Kintetsu 1-day ¥1,900 only if you do Nara and Kyoto on Kintetsu the same day). Onsen: Spa World and many sento refuse tattoos, including stickers. Spa World adds ¥1,300 after midnight. Year-end: Osaka Castle closes 28 Dec, which is after this leg, so not a problem.
